newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge orders Donnelley to keep records.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge orders Donnelley to keep records.

text.p: A U.S. District Court judge Wednesday ordered printer R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co. to save materials that might relate to a pending class action race discrimination lawsuit involving more than 500 black workers.

Judge Ann Williams verbally issued the interim order to maintain the records, and said the plaintiffs' request for a formal injunction regarding the records would be considered by a U.S. magistrate, attorney Candace Gorman said.

Donnelley spokesman Bill Lowe said managers were already told earlier this month to maintain records that included e-mail, computerized messages, and graffiti after plaintiffs in the lawsuit charged evidence was being destroyed.
He said Judge Williams applauded the company's efforts so far to maintain its records.

The lawsuit on behalf of about 550 black former employees, about 400 of them from Chicago-area plants, alleged that Donnelley exhibited a pattern of discrimination in employment practices and allowed racial harrassment in its plants. The suit could ask for damages in excess of $500 million.
The company reiterated that the suit has no merit.

The suit contends that black workers were routinely laid off at higher rates than white employees, and black layoffs were used to keep long-time employees from achieving full-time status and benefits. The suit also charged Donnelley managers exchanged racially-charged memos and jokes.
